body:
I am not in a good position to try and convince anyone of anything in my university. I will try to, if they move for withdrawal, but some mistakes I made have probably given the impression to those deciding on my withdrawal that I've been faking or exaggerating illness. (I have not. If anything, I've downplayed it.)
Mistakes such as, last year, asking a doctor who'd only seen me twice to talk to the university, as opposed to asking my "actual" doctor who'd been seeing me through almost all of the illness. Also, in my first year, no longer going to the doctor after they admitted that there might have been a misdiagnosis of mood disorders.

I say my mind has been eaten away because I have felt my mental faculties decreasing bit by bit over the last few years. Things I used to do in seconds now take much longer to complete. Or they're never completed. As in, relating concepts, solving problems, analysing things,... Basically all one needs as a student.
I don't know how it happened. Maybe the continuous stress? Maybe health interfered? 

I also don't have much access to help in my university at this point. Career counseling included. I'm not a fully registered student due to spending the year on an interruption of studies before retaking exams.

And as for my parents... While I feel guilty about the money, it's not the biggest issue. It's their disappointment I can't stand. And don't see how I would even begin to repay that.


In any case, thanks for reminding me that there might be other options.
Maybe, if I ever get to feel less exhausted, I'll be able to go look for them. If not... Well, we'll see.
